title.en: What a bill of exchange is

body.en: Under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, a bill of exchange is an instrument in writing containing an unconditional order, signed by the maker, directing a certain person to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person or to the bearer. The seller (creditor) draws the bill and the buyer (debtor) accepts it by signing across it. Once accepted, the bill is a legal and transferable proof of the debt.

points.en: Drawer: the person who writes the bill (the creditor)
Drawee: the person ordered to pay; after signing, the acceptor
Payee: the person who receives the money (often the drawer)
The order is unconditional and the amount is certain
It must be stamped and signed

title.en: Promissory notes and the due date

body.en: A promissory note is written by the debtor himself: an unconditional promise to pay a certain sum to a certain person. It has two parties, the maker and the payee, and needs no acceptance. For a bill payable some time after date, the term is added to the date of drawing and three days of grace are then added to get the date of maturity. If that date is a public holiday, the bill is due on the preceding business day; if it is an emergency holiday declared suddenly, it is due on the next business day.

points.en: Bill: an order, three parties, needs acceptance
Note: a promise, two parties, no acceptance
Due date = date + term + 3 days of grace
For the drawer it is a bill receivable; for the drawee a bill payable

problem.en: Ravi draws a bill on Meena on 10 April 2026 for ₹30,000 payable 60 days after date. Meena accepts it. Find the due date. Who records it as a bill receivable?

steps.en: When the term is in days, count days and leave out the day of drawing.
April: 30 − 10 = 20 days; May: 31 days (51); June: 9 more days make 60, which ends the term on 9 June.
Ravi, the drawer, records a bill receivable; Meena records a bill payable.

answer.en: Due on 12 June 2026; Ravi treats it as a bill receivable and Meena as a bill payable.

heading.en: Months by calendar, days by counting

body.en: A term in months: jump to the same date in the later month (or its last day). A term in days: count the days, excluding the date of drawing. Then always add 3 days of grace.

points.en: A bill of exchange is an unconditional written order; a promissory note is an unconditional written promise.
A bill has three parties: drawer, drawee and payee; a note has two: maker and payee.
Due date = date of drawing + term + 3 days of grace.
A public holiday moves the due date to the preceding business day.
